sections.overview: Edonis helena is the sole described species in the dragonfly genus Edonis, with records from Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina.
sections.identification: An identification key separates Edonis by a dark basal patch on the hindwing reaching the triangle and two bridge crossveins in the forewing.
sections.habitat: Its habitat and larval stages remain unknown in the taxonomic account cited by the literature.
sections.diet: Species-specific prey and feeding observations were not found in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: The available regional records are too limited to describe its daily activity or seasonal behaviour.
sections.reproduction: No species-specific account of egg-laying or larval development was found; the larva remains undescribed in the cited reference.
sections.ecology: The Chaco Odonata review notes that the species is still known from very few collected specimens, including its original description and later Argentine records.
sections.conservation: Brazil’s 2014 national assessment listed it as Data Deficient; that regional category is not a global Red List assessment.
